title: PET and polyethylene film
description: Polivac film composed of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) laminated to polyethylene film, used for packaging products
blurb: A laminate of two plastics. Which one gives the essential character?
reference_excerpt: The product in question is Polivac film, which is specifically described as being composed of a layer of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film laminated to a layer of polyethylene film. The ruling indicates that the PET film constitutes 60 percent by weight and the polyethylene film 40 percent by weight. According to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), the applicable tariff provision for such products is 3920.62.0000.

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 3920 covers noncellular plastic film not reinforced, laminated or similarly combined with other materials. The laminate is all plastic, so 3921 does not apply.
GRI 3(b): the PET/PE laminate is prima facie classifiable under both 3920.62 (PET) and 3920.10 (PE). I assumed PET gives the essential character, because it is the named structural layer.
GRI 6: 3920.62 (of poly(ethylene terephthalate)), then the 'Other' line, because the film is not metallized and is not gift wrap.

classification.rationale: Heading 3920 covers all-plastic laminated film under GRI 1. I assumed the PET layer gives the composite its essential character under GRI 3(b), which places it in 3920.62. It is not metallized or gift wrap, so the 'Other' line 3920.62.00.90 applies, consistent with N326371. If the PE layer predominates, the code would be 3920.10.00.00 instead.
